narrative: Demand for PL2__MD0B3E34 is high-volume and smooth (CV=0.377) with a statistically significant upward trend of ~112 units/day. Current SAP policy carries no safety stock, leaving the 95% service level target unmet. An (r,Q) policy is recommended: the unconstrained EOQ of 595,138 units was capped to 457,499 units by the 483,615-unit storage ceiling, yielding 12 annual orders versus the SAP baseline of 63, and introducing a data-driven safety stock of 26,116 units for adequate demand and lead-time buffer coverage.
warnings: EOQ (595,138) exceeds storage capacity (483,615). Order quantity capped to 457,499 units. Slightly increases ordering frequency vs unconstrained optimum.
Significant upward demand trend detected (p=0.0003, slope=+112 units/day). Mean demand used for EOQ may understate future requirements; recommend re-running analysis in 3 months.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth demand pattern (CV=0.377), 100% non-zero days, and normally-distributed working-day demand make the classical (r,Q) EOQ model the most appropriate and cost-efficient replenishment framework. No intermittent-demand adjustments required.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity cap reduces order quantity from unconstrained EOQ of 595,138 to 457,499 units, increasing annual order count from ~9.6 to ~12.4. Annual cost impact is modest (+ordering cost offset) but service level is preserved. Recommend reviewing storage allocation if upward demand trend continues.
